title: A tiny file system
description:
A disk is a list of **blocks**; here each block is a string of exactly 4 characters. A file system's table maps each file name to `(list of block numbers, size in characters)`. The blocks of a file can be anywhere on the disk, in any order.

```python
def read_file(disk, table, name)     # the file's text: its blocks joined in order, cut to its size; None if there is no such file
def free_blocks(disk, table)         # the numbers of the blocks no file uses, smallest first
```

```python
disk = ["Hell", "xxxx", "o, w", "orld", "Bye!"]
table = {"hello.txt": ([0, 2, 3], 12), "bye.txt": ([4], 3)}
read_file(disk, table, "hello.txt")    # "Hello, world"
read_file(disk, table, "bye.txt")      # "Bye"   (the size cuts off the !)
free_blocks(disk, table)               # [1]
```

`"".join(parts)` glues strings together; `text[:size]` keeps the first `size` characters.
